rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a high-entropy spinel oxide support with isolated PGM sites, whereas the target paper used a closed-loop high-throughput campaign to iteratively select composition and synthesis parameters for multi-element alloy catalysts on La-doped alumina. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (support design vs. composition/process optimization).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies dry, lean exhaust conditions, while the target paper used a near-stoichiometric feed with cyclic lean/rich ageing and a complex gas mixture including NO, CO, hydrocarbons, and water. The regimes are different (lean vs. stoichiometric/rich cycling).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes entropy-stabilized oxide lattice, oxygen vacancies, and sintering resistance to explain performance. The target paper's mechanism involves electronic redistribution, Cu-Pt cooperative sites, and redox coupling between hydrocarbon oxidation and NO reduction. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a lower light-off temperature and improved durability with reduced PGM loading. The target paper predicted and found that inverse-model-guided selection yields catalysts with superior post-ageing low-temperature and total conversion relative to a Pd baseline. Both predict improved catalytic performance, but the specific property (light-off T10 vs. T50/conversion at 350 °C) and the nature of the improvement differ.
